path: Four page body sections that the catalog lacks: the opening of an article, a single pull quote, a contact panel, and a day-grouped event schedule. Each renders the page's own content rather than replacing it, keeps its actions as real links, buttons, or form controls, and composes at most three cores from earlier waves. They are public page idioms and plain semantic HTML patterns rather than re-implementations of any particular work, so they are originated and carry no credits, and nothing here is built from a capture, a shortlist, or anyone's component. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, every default is a pure function of its props, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one. All design, building, and review of this wave runs through Claude CLI sessions.

components.title: Article Lead
components.brief:
The opening of an article on a content page: a mono dateline above, the page's own headline and standfirst in a reading measure, and a ruled column of article facts beside it. The page supplies the headline and the standfirst as children, at the heading size the page already uses. The core adds only what the page does not already carry. Above the children sits a dateline row holding the section name and the publication date as a real time element with a datetime attribute. Beside or below them sits an aside holding a semantic dl with the rows Words by, Published, and Read time, followed by an In brief list of up to three key points as an ol. Structure at 1280 px: a two column grid. The first column holds the dateline and the children and is held to a measure of about 62 characters with the ch unit, so the standfirst never runs wider than a line a reader can follow. The second column is about 15rem wide, separated from the first by a single 1px vertical rule, and holds the facts and the key points, each row divided by a hairline. The first paragraph the page supplies is set about one step larger than body text and in the page's font, as a lead, through a scoped child selector that changes no markup. Structure at 390 px: one column in this order, dateline, the children, then the aside, with the vertical rule replaced by a 1px top rule, every line wrapping within the host and nothing overflowing sideways or clipping. Look: hairlines, square corners, no card, shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Headline, standfirst, author names, and key points inherit the page's font and size. The dateline, the dl labels, the read time figure, and the numbers in the In brief list use mono, uppercase and tracked for labels, with tabular figures. Only one thing uses the accent: a short 2rem accent rule above the dateline. The accent never sets text on paper. Any focusable element added by future data gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only, and a disabled native control is shown at 45% opacity. Dates are formatted by hand in UTC from fixed English month tables, never through a locale, so both generated shapes print the same text. It reads no clock. The core never hides, moves, rewrites, or draws over the page's children, adds its own nodes only before and after them, and removes them on destroy. Why a measure matters.

Sixty characters is where a line stops being a guess and starts being a reading habit, and every other choice on the page answers to it.

The paragraphs below hold to the same width.

. Difference from a sibling: editorial-hero, shipped in wave 9, is a magazine spread that sets its own deck, a headline much larger than anything near it, a drop capital, a byline between hairlines, an optional composed image, and action links, and it takes the headline as a prop. article-lead takes the headline from the page at the page's own size, has no deck, drop capital, image, or actions, and exists to carry the article's facts and key points beside a readable measure. Existing Picagram reference: follow registry/sections/editorial-hero for the scoped stylesheet, the flow minimum, and how a section adds nodes around the page's children without touching them, and registry/sections/stats-kpi for the mono tabular figure treatment. Capture targets: a 1280 px frame shows the dateline with its accent rule, the headline and a two paragraph standfirst in a measure of about 62 characters, and a populated right column with three facts and three key points, so neither column is empty ground. A 390 px frame shows the single column order with the aside beneath the children, every row legible. It is wrong if the headline is set in a display size larger than the page's own heading, because that is editorial-hero; if the standfirst runs wider than about 70 characters at 1280 px; if the aside is an empty bordered column when authors or points are cleared, because an empty list must remove its row or its whole group rather than leave a frame; if dates are produced through a locale or the clock so two shapes disagree; if the time element has no datetime; if the accent sets any text; or if mobile keeps two squeezed columns. Section rules, restated because a builder starts with nothing: the host keeps its role and its children and is never hidden; every node the core adds carries data-pica; the host's attributes and styles are restored on destroy; destroy twice is harmless; data-pica-ready is set after the first complete draw and deleted on destroy; a scoped stylesheet selects by the data-pica-id attribute and never by class; colors come only from the palette through cssVar and cssOn; it draws nothing behind the content and mounts no background; and it composes no cores. The 16384 byte sections budget includes shared runtime and any composed core. Expect about 4.5 KB gzipped with shared runtime because this composes none. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from createRng, createNoise, or hashSeed with the seed, though this design needs none, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: section (string, default "ESSAY"), date (string, an ISO date, default "2026-09-14"), authors (json, [{ name, role }], default two invented people: Mara Quill, Editor, and Jonas Reed, Design), readingTime (number, 0 to 60 minutes, default 8, 0 removes the row), points (json string array of up to three key points, default three complete sentences about measure, rhythm, and restraint, an empty array removes the In brief group), pointsLabel (string, default "In brief"), label (string, default "Article details", the accessible name of the aside), measure (number, 48 to 80 ch, default 62). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Quote Band
components.brief:
One pull quote set large across a band of the page, with its attribution and nothing else. The core builds a figure that holds a blockquote and a figcaption, so the quotation and its source are one semantic unit. The quote text comes from props. Any children the page supplies sit above the figure as a short lead in and are left untouched. Structure at 1280 px: a band with a 1px rule above and below. Inside it, a left gutter holds a tall hairline running the height of the quote, and the accent colors the top 2rem of that hairline only. To its right the quote is set in the page's own font at a large size, between about 1.75rem and 3rem by clamp, in a balanced wrap through text-wrap: balance, held to a measure of about 28em, so it breaks into three or four even lines rather than one long line. Below it, after a short 2rem rule drawn as a row of box drawing glyphs, the attribution reads name in the page's font and role in mono, uppercase and tracked. If an href is given the name is a real a[href] and the blockquote carries it as its cite attribute, otherwise the name is plain text. The opening and closing quotation marks are drawn as aria-hidden glyph spans, so assistive technology reads the quote itself and not the marks. An optional quiet dot-lattice composed from registry/patterns/dot-lattice draws behind the band through layer(host, "under"), at a low strength and fading toward the edges, so the type is always the louder layer, and it is hidden from assistive technology. Structure at 390 px: the gutter hairline moves to a 1px rule above the quote, the type drops to the clamp's floor, the quote wraps within the host with no overflow or clipping, and the attribution stacks name over role. With align set to center the gutter is dropped, the quote and attribution are centered, and the rules stay. Look: hairlines, square corners, no card, shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Only the hairline's accent segment uses the accent, and the accent never sets text on paper. The link, when present, gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only and a roughly 10% fg tint on hover. State changes are instant and nothing moves. components.title: Contact Panel
components.brief:
A page section that shows how to reach someone and offers a short message form, without sending anything anywhere. The page supplies its heading and introduction as children. The core adds two regions below them. The first is a contact details list: a semantic dl in which each channel is a dt label and a dd value. A channel with an href renders its value as a real a[href], such as mailto: or tel:, and a channel without one renders plain text, with an address held in an address element. The second is a form with an accessible name from label, holding three visible, labelled controls: a text input named name, an input of type email named email, and a textarea named message, then a submit button, a mono note, and a status region. The form never posts or calls the network. On submit it calls preventDefault, and if the native constraint validation fails it calls reportValidity and emits nothing. If it passes it emits send with { name, email, message } and writes the confirmation text into the status region, which has role status and aria-live polite, so the result is announced without moving focus. The fields keep their values after a send. Controls are native elements styled like the catalog's: follow registry/ui/input and registry/ui/textarea for their treatment, but build them in this core and do not import them. Structure at 1280 px: the children span the full width, and below them two columns. The left column, about a third of the width, holds the channels as rows divided by hairlines, label in mono above value. The right column holds the form, with name and email side by side in one row and the message beneath, the button left aligned under the message with the note beside it. Structure at 390 px: a single column, details first, then the form with every control stacked at full width, the focus outline fully visible, and nothing overflowing sideways or clipping. Look: one 1px line around each control, square corners, no shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners, and no card around the panel. Heading, introduction, labels, input text, and the button label inherit the page's font. Channel labels and the note use mono. The submit button is the single filled accent surface with readable cssOn text, and the accent is never input text or any text on paper. Every link and control gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only. Hover is limited to a roughly 10% fg mix and state changes are instant. When disabled is true every control and the button are disabled and shown at 45% opacity, never hidden. The defaults prefill the three fields with a complete valid example so the interaction can be judged and verified at once. The core never hides, moves, or draws over the page's children, adds its own nodes after them, and removes them on destroy. It composes no cores and draws nothing behind the content. Set meta.wave to 11, meta.facets to ["static", "interactive", "text"], meta.palette to ["fg", "muted", "accent"], meta.host to "div", meta.stage to "flow", and meta.wraps to "content". Omit meta.controlled. components.title: Event Schedule
components.brief:
A readable agenda for an event, grouped by day. The page supplies its heading and introduction as children. The core builds one group per distinct day from JSON, [{ day, start, end, title, speaker, place, href }], in date order and then start order, with ties kept in input order. Each group is a section element named by a heading, with the heading level taken from headingLevel so it fits under whatever heading the page already has, followed by an ol of sessions. Each session is an li holding a time element with a datetime attribute for its start, the title, and a line of speaker and place. If a session has an href its title is a real a[href], otherwise it is plain text. Times are printed exactly as given, as wall clock text, and are never converted, and a zone caption from zone sits once above the first day. Structure at 1280 px: each day is a row of two columns. The left column, about 11rem wide, holds the weekday in mono, uppercase and tracked, with the day of the month and month name beneath it, set in the page's font at a size larger than the sessions. The right column holds the sessions, each a row divided from the next by a hairline, with the start time in mono in a narrow first cell and the end time in muted mono beneath it, then the title, then the speaker and place in muted below it. A 1px rule separates day from day. The highlighted session is marked with an accent bar on its left edge, a visible label from highlightLabel in mono before its title, and nothing else, so the marker is never color alone. Structure at 390 px: the day label stacks above its sessions, the time moves above the title inside each row, long titles and places wrap within the host, and nothing overflows sideways or clips. The default frame holds two days with three fully populated sessions each. Look: hairlines, square corners, no card, shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Titles and speakers inherit the page's font. Weekday, times, the zone caption, and the highlight label use mono with tabular figures. The accent marks only the highlighted session's bar and never sets text on paper. Dates are formatted by hand in UTC from fixed English weekday and month tables, so both generated shapes print the same text, and the core never reads the clock, so nothing is marked as happening now. A link gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only and a roughly 10% fg tint on hover. A session with an empty title is skipped, and an empty list leaves a single muted line of text rather than an empty frame. . The core never hides, moves, rewrites, or draws over those children, adds its own nodes after them, and removes them on destroy. It composes no cores. Difference from a sibling: the shipped timeline-chart plots spans and point events against a measured time axis, offers an SVG and a glyph look, and carries a hidden data table, so position carries the data. The reserved milestone-timeline is an ordered run of dated milestones with no day grouping and no clock times. The shipped calendar in registry/ui is a month grid of day cells for choosing a date. event-schedule has no axis, no duration bars, no grid of days, and no chart role, and it is plain text arranged so that someone can find their next session. Existing Picagram reference: follow registry/sections/stats-kpi for the section grid, the mono tabular figures, and the responsive column rules, and registry/data/timeline-chart only for how its dates are parsed in UTC, not for how it draws. Capture targets: a 1280 px frame shows two day rows each with a day label column and three populated sessions, one session with the accent bar and its visible label, and the zone caption above. A 390 px frame shows the stacked layout with times above titles and every line wrapped.
